response_body.answer: Both string sets consist of nickel plated steel electric guitar strings that resist tone-deadening corrosion and sound fresh for a long time. The difference lies in their coating: Nanoweb coating makes the strings sound brighter, while Polyweb coating makes them sound warmer. Polyweb strings feel slick and fast, whereas Nanoweb strings have a smooth feeling. The video suggests testing different strings back to back to determine which one sounds and feels better for you.

# NANOWEB vs POLYWEB - which strings sound better? | GUITAR Q&A SHOW #11
## Channel: BERNTH (verified)
1.56M subscribers
1K likes

### Description
91,549 views
Posted: 2018-06-25
In this week's guitar Q&A show we compare Nanoweb to Polyweb strings. Which strings sound better to you? Could you hear the difference? Thanks a lot to Elixir strings for sending over so many sets for the upcoming tour and studio dates!

FACEBOOK PAGE — I post videos, exercises and Q&A sessions on this page: http://fb.com/bernthofficial

QUESTION — You have a question about technique, theory, gear, career or anything else? Post it in the  comments of this video!

Bernth Brodträger on Social Media:
http://www.bernth.at
  / bernthofficial  
  / bernthofficial  

About this video:
In this week's Q&A show Bernth talks about the difference between Nanoweb and Polyweb strings.

### Transcript
[0:00] Hi, Bernth here!
[0:01] Welcome to episode 11 of my weekly guitar Q&A series, this time I would like to show you the difference between Nanoweb and Polyweb strings.
[0:18] First off all I want to thank Elixir for sending me so many different string sets for the upcoming tour and studio dates.
[0:25] I already talked about them in the first Q&A video and got a couple of questions concerning the different types of strings they make.
[0:33] Today I want to compare the Nanoweb and Polyweb sets.
[0:37] I will show you a direct comparison using the same guitar and recording equipment for both. Let's talk about the details first.
[0:44] Both string sets consist of nickel plated steel electric guitar strings. They sound fresh for a very long time and resist tone-deadening corrosion.
[0:52] Elixir is also the only coated string brand to protect the entire string with an ultra-thin coating. That is exactly where the difference between these two string sets lies.
[1:02] The easy way to remember is that Nanoweb coating makes the strings sound more bright, Polyweb coating makes them sound warm.
[1:09] What I can't show you in this video is how they feel. I never actually took time to test them back to back and was quite surprised by the difference.
[1:17] Polyweb coated strings feel slick & fast while Nanoweb coated strings have a smooth feeling to them.
[1:23] To help you decide which one you should go for, I recorded some chords, licks and riffs for a side by side comparison, check it out.
[2:28] As you can hopefully hear there is a very slight difference in sound with these examples.
[2:33] Not a drastic change but you do hear that the Nanoweb coated strings sound a bight brighter and the Polyweb strings sound a bit more warm.
[2:42] You hear it best with the clean & DI track examples, especially with the two short solo licks I played.
[2:48] I really recommend to test different strings back to back this way, it's also very important see which ones feel better for you.
[2:55] As for the string gauge, I used 10s for this video and played my Ibanez Artist guitar - not the fanciest guitar I own, so probably the right one to go for a simple and realistic test.
[3:05] If want like to dig even deeper, Elixir have a great tool on their website to further compare their different products.
[3:11] You can compare them to uncoated strings and also to their new and crisp Optiweb strings.
[3:17] That's all we have time for this week, I'd love to know which strings you preferred and if you could hear the difference.
[3:23] Leave a comment and tell us which strings you like to play or send me a question for the next episode! Thanks a lot for watching!
